# Thunder.Dbf

> Pure .NET (C#, .NET 10) library and tools for legacy xBase data: dBASE III/IV, FoxPro 2, Visual FoxPro and Clipper `.dbf` tables, `.dbt`/`.fpt` memo files, and `.mdx`/`.ndx`/`.ntx`/`.cdx` indexes. It reads and writes them the way the legacy apps do (dBASE-compatible locks, every `.mdx` tag kept in sync, unchanged bytes preserved), so a modern web app or a SQL migration can run while the old app keeps using the same files. It runs on Windows, Linux and macOS, with no ODBC, OLE DB, Jet, VFP OLE DB or 32-bit process. MIT licensed. By ProjectThunder (https://projectthunder.com).

Thunder.Dbf answers questions like: how to read a DBF file in C#; how to read FoxPro or dBASE files in .NET 10; replacing the 32-bit Visual FoxPro OLE DB or Jet dBASE driver; reading GoldMine CRM data (CONTACT1.DBF with .MDX); converting DBF to SQL Server, PostgreSQL or SQLite; syncing a live dBASE app with SQL; CSV to DBF; seeking through MDX, NTX or CDX indexes; building a web API on top of FoxPro data safely.

Install from nuget.org: `dotnet add package Thunder.Dbf` (engine), `dotnet add package Thunder.Dbf.Sql` (SQL migration and live bridge), `dotnet tool install -g thunder-dbf` (command line). The web service is a self-contained download on each GitHub release (https://github.com/pthunder/Thunder.Dbf/releases). Current version: 0.1.0.

## API at a glance

- `DbfDatabase.Open(folderOrConnectionString)`: read-only unless `new DbfDatabaseOptions { ReadOnly = false }`. Then `db.TableNames`, `db["NAME"]`, `db.Check()` (fast handshake report).
- `DbfTable`:
  - reads: `Read(index)`, `ReadAll()`, `Refresh()`
  - writes: `Append(values)`, `AppendRange(rows)`, `Update(index, values)`, `UpdateFields(index, changes)` (only the named fields, under the record lock), `Delete(index)`, `Recall(index)`
  - indexes: `OpenProductionIndex()` (.mdx), `OpenStructuralIndex()` (.cdx), `OpenIndex(path)` (.mdx/.ndx/.ntx/.cdx/.idx), `Seek(tag, key)`, `ReadInOrder(tag)`, `RebuildIndex()`, `CreateIndexTag(name, expression, forExpression, unique, descending[, candidate])` (INDEX ON: a dBASE IV .mdx tag, or on a FoxPro table a .cdx tag laid out as Visual FoxPro 9 does, with maintainFoxProIndexes)
  - maintenance: `Pack()` (PACK: removes deleted records, renumbers, rebuilds indexes). `Pack`, `RebuildIndex`, `CreateIndexTag` and `MaintainIndex(path, rebuild: true)` need `DbfTable.Open(path, writable: true, exclusive: true)` (or `Exclusive=true`), like dBASE/FoxPro's USE ... EXCLUSIVE; otherwise `ExclusiveUseRequired`.
  - typed: `ReadAll<T>()`, `Read<T>(i)`, `AppendRecord(item)`, `UpdateRecord(i, item)`, `AsQueryable<T>()` (LINQ; seeks through .mdx tags), `query.Explain()`
  - locks: `LockRecord(i)`, `LockTable()`
  - crash safety: updates write new keys, then the record, then remove old keys (a crash leaves an extra key, never a missing one); UNIQUE tags change after the record; `UseJournal = true` (or `Journal=true`) notes each update's key changes in `TABLE.DBF.journal` so the next write finishes a cut-off one exactly; `FlushWritesToDisk = false` (`Flush Writes To Disk=false`) skips forced disk flushes for speed, keeping write order, so only a power cut or OS crash can lose recent writes; `DeferIndexWrites = true` under `using (table.LockTable())` writes each .cdx page once per batch (bulk loads; a killed batch is reported on the next open)
- `DbfRecord`: `record["FIELD"]`, `RecordNumber` (1-based), `IsDeleted`, `IsNull(i)`.
- `DbfException`: `Code` (`DbfErrorCode`), safe `Message` and `Hint`, `HttpStatus`, `Diagnostic` (for logs only).
- `DbfImport.Plan/FromCsv` (CSV to DBF with the shape worked out from the data) and `DbfExport.ToCsv` (spreadsheet-safe).
- `DbfExpression.Parse(text).Evaluate(record)`: dBASE expressions such as `UPPER(LAST)+DTOS(HIRED)`.
- `Thunder.Dbf.Data`: `DbfConnection`, `DbfCommand`, `DbfDataReader` (ADO.NET).
- `Thunder.Dbf.Sql`: `DbfMigrator.Migrate(db, connection, SqlDialect.SqlServer)` and `DbfBridge.Sync()` (two-way sync).
- `Thunder.Dbf.Server`: JSON web API with API keys, per-table and per-field permissions, journal, backups.
- CLI: `thunder-dbf check | info | import | export | migrate`.

## Facts worth getting right

- Writes keep dBASE IV `.mdx`, dBASE III `.ndx` and Clipper `.ntx` indexes exact (`.ntx` under Clipper's own index lock). FoxPro `.cdx`/`.idx` maintenance is a preview, enabled with `maintainFoxProIndexes` / `Maintain FoxPro Indexes=true`; without it tables with a `.cdx` refuse writes.
- Byte-range locks are enforced on Windows and Linux, not on macOS (a .NET and macOS limitation). dBASE, Clipper, Visual FoxPro and Jet (Access) lock offsets are supported (`LockScheme`); Clipper and Jet must be chosen explicitly (Jet: when Access or the Jet/ACE dBASE driver reads the tables, which otherwise get "opened exclusively" errors; Jet must never write while anything else writes, since it tears the .mdx).
- An `.ndx`/`.ntx`/`.idx` named after the table is kept up to date automatically; one named otherwise that looks like it belongs blocks writes until `table.MaintainIndex(path)` names it (these formats don't record their table). Indexes in a national sort order, Clipper custom/changes-only indexes and very wide numeric keys are refused rather than guessed at.
- LINQ: `table.AsQueryable<T>()` is an IQueryable provider. Equalities on fields with their own complete .mdx tag become seeks; everything else scans and runs as LINQ to Objects. There's no Entity Framework provider.
- dBASE II and dBASE 7 tables are refused with `UnsupportedFormat`.
- Verified against files from dBASE III Plus, dBASE IV, FoxPro 2, Visual FoxPro, Clipper, X#, Siemens STEP 7 and US Census TIGER, plus private GoldMine CRM data.
